story.titleZh: 维斯塔潘2026年梅赛德斯接触与去年截然不同
story.summaryZh: 在赞德沃特的年度媒体会上，梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫被荷兰记者问及维斯塔潘是否会加盟梅赛德斯。此次沃尔夫表示大门看似关闭，但仍留有一丝余地。
story.originalTitle: Why Verstappen's 2026 Mercedes contact was very different from last year's
story.summaryEn: At his annual media session with Dutch journalists in Zandvoort, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was asked whether Max Verstappen would join Mercedes. This time Wolff said the door looks closed, though he keeps it ever so slightly ajar.
detailZh: 为什么维斯塔潘2026年与梅赛德斯的接触与去年截然不同
梅赛德斯与乔治·拉塞尔和基米·安东内利续约至2027年，红牛也与马克斯·维斯塔潘续约；如今，托托·沃尔夫认为，他要再过几年才会有下一次抢走这位四届世界冠军的机会。
马克斯·维斯塔潘究竟会不会在F1中为梅赛德斯效力？这是车队领队托托·沃尔夫在赞德沃特与荷兰记者举行的年度媒体会上被问到的问题——而这一次，大门看似关闭，尽管沃尔夫仍把它留了一丝缝。
如果梅赛德斯在2014年击败红牛，锁定这位年轻人的未来，F1的历史可能会完全不同。当时维斯塔潘作为单座赛车新秀在F3中不断赢下比赛，但他的目标坚定地锁定在立即完成世界冠军赛首秀上。这是只有红牛才能提供的机会，凭借其第二支车队。
自那以后，梅赛德斯和维斯塔潘一直是对手，但两年前，沃尔夫透露他曾与当时的三届世界冠军进行过会谈。这位奥地利人面临着为即将转投法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿寻找合适替代者的艰巨任务，并且已经把目光投向了下一代天才基米·安东内利，但如果签下维斯塔潘有一丝可能实现，他显然不会放过这个机会。
最终没有实现，但当Autosport问沃尔夫，是否仍会在心里考虑潜在签下维斯塔潘时，沃尔夫坚称大门并未关闭：“是的，会。不知怎的，我有那种感觉。但我不知道那会是什么时候。是26年，还是三年后，我还不知道。”
一年后，随着新秀安东内利在首个赛季中挣扎，沃尔夫再次试探了维斯塔潘，但这位红牛车手再次向位于米尔顿凯恩斯的车队承诺忠诚。
“这是否意味着因为时机不对，我们的道路永远不会交汇？嗯，那是可能发生的，”沃尔夫当时思索道。“但那可能是50%。另外50%是，我们会在各自职业生涯的某个阶段一起比赛，如果这对双方都合适的话。”
但如今，沃尔夫承认，在6月确认拉塞尔和安东内利将在2027年继续效力银箭之后，他看不到维斯塔潘会在短期内加盟梅赛德斯；与此同时，这位荷兰人的新红牛合同在他主场赛前公布——尽管维斯塔潘目前正经历自2015年以来首个无胜赛季。
“很早我们就觉得，与乔治和基米继续合作是正确的决定——出于各种原因，但看起来这套车手阵容就是正确的积极动态，”沃尔夫评论道。“它让基米得以成长，也让乔治发挥出最佳水平，因为他有一位速度很快的年轻队友。
“因此，马克斯留在红牛看起来相当合乎逻辑。熟悉的魔鬼总比未知的好——这是个包袱！——然后再等两三年看看会发生什么，届时合同会再次打开，可能他的选择不只是一支车队，而是一次有三四支。然后等着看谁表现最好。”
当Autosport问梅赛德斯是否曾有任何机会为2027年签下维斯塔潘时，沃尔夫解释道：“在晚春很早就清楚，我们会按现在的方式继续。我们之间有着开放、在某种程度上尽可能透明的关系。所以，正如你所说，情况与去年非常不同，当时双方都在探索合作是否可能发生。”
维斯塔潘新合同的公布结束了关于这位四届世界冠军未来的猜测，此前他在车手中堪称对F1新规最持批评态度的人之一。关于要做出“人生”决定的隐晦、随口之言，加上他参与GT3赛事，助长了谣言，但最终，红牛的超级明星决定继续他的F1生涯。
当被问及是否对维斯塔潘在该系列赛中留得更久感到惊讶时，沃尔夫说：“不。规则越成熟，车队就越会追赶上来。即使红牛目前处于下风，也很清楚，给它一些时间，他们会闪耀。
“他们今年有过强劲的比赛，也有过不好的。但我毫不怀疑，未来通常的那些竞争者会再次为胜利和冠军而战，无论是法拉利、迈凯伦、红牛还是我们自己。所以这个决定在我看来某种程度上是合乎逻辑的。”
detailEn: Why Verstappen's 2026 Mercedes contact was very different from last year's

Mercedes extended its deals with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli for 2027, and so did Red Bull with Max Verstappen; by now, Toto Wolff believes it will be a few years until he gets another chance to snatch the four-time champion away

Will Max Verstappen ever race for Mercedes in Formula 1? This is what team principal Toto Wolff is quizzed about in his yearly media session with Dutch journalists at Zandvoort – and this time the door looks closed, though Wolff keeps it ever so slightly ajar.

F1’s history could have panned out very differently if Mercedes had beaten Red Bull to secure the youngster’s future back in 2014, as Verstappen kept winning races in Formula 3 as a single-seater rookie, but his sights were firmly set on an immediate world championship debut. That’s something only Red Bull could offer, courtesy of its second outfit.

Since then, Mercedes and Verstappen have always been rivals, but two years ago, Wolff revealed he had held talks with the then-three-time world champion. The Austrian faced the tall order of finding a worthy replacement for Ferrari-bound Lewis Hamilton and had already set his sights on next-generation wunderkind Kimi Antonelli, but he obviously wouldn’t have passed on the opportunity of recruiting Verstappen, had it had the slightest chance of materialising.

It didn’t, but Wolff insisted the door was not closed, when asked by Autosport if a potential move for Verstappen was still in the back of his mind: “Yes, it is. Somehow I have that feeling. But I don't know when that could be. Whether it's '26, whether it's three years later, I don't know yet.”
Wolff again sounded out Verstappen one year later, as rookie Antonelli struggled in his maiden season, but the Red Bull racer pledged loyalty anew to the Milton Keynes-based team.

“Could that mean our paths will never cross because the timings are wrong? Well, that can happen,” Wolff pondered at the time. “But that could be 50%. The other 50% is we are racing together at a certain stage in our careers, if it is right for both sides.”

But by now, Wolff admits he can’t see Verstappen joining Mercedes anytime soon, after Russell and Antonelli were confirmed in the Silver Arrows for 2027 back in June, while the Dutchman’s new Red Bull deal was announced ahead of his home race – despite Verstappen currently going through his first winless campaign since 2015.

“Pretty early we felt for us that being with George and Kimi was the right decision to continue – for various reasons, but it seems that the driver line-up is just the right positive dynamic,” Wolff commented. “It allows Kimi to grow and for George to bring out his best game because he has a quick, young team-mate.

“Therefore it seemed pretty logical that Max would stay with Red Bull. Better the devil you know – that's a punchline! – and then wait what happens in two or three years, where contracts open up again and probably his options are not just one team but maybe three or four at a time. And wait who performs the best.”

Asked by Autosport if Mercedes had had any chance at all of hiring Verstappen for 2027, Wolff explained: “Pretty early in the late spring it was clear that we would continue like we do. And we have an open and in a way most transparent relationship as we can have. So the situation, as you say, was very different to what it was last year, where both sides were exploring whether cooperation could happen or not.”

The announcement of Verstappen’s new contract ended speculation over the four-time world champion’s future, after he emerged among drivers as arguably the most critical of F1’s new regulations. Cryptic, throwaway lines about “life” decisions to make fuelled rumours amid his involvement in GT3 racing, but in the end, Red Bull’s superstar decided to keep his F1 career going.

Asked if he was surprised to see Verstappen staying longer in the series, Wolff said: “No. The more regulations mature the more the teams will catch up. And even if Red Bull at the moment is on the back foot it is clear that, give it some time, they will shine.

“They have had strong races this year, others that were not. But I have no doubt that going forward the usual suspects will be again fighting for wins and championships, whether it is Ferrari or McLaren or Red Bull or ourselves. So the decision’s in a way logical one for me.”

detailZh: F1卡塔尔大奖赛：乔治·拉塞尔击败安东内利夺得杆位
乔治·拉塞尔在2026年第六次夺得杆位，梅赛德斯车队在F1卡塔尔大奖赛的预赛中全面领先。
乔治·拉塞尔在F1卡塔尔大奖赛中夺得杆位，击败队友安东内利，梅赛德斯车队在多哈的比赛中全面领先。
在卢塞尔赛道的高下压力赛道上，梅赛德斯车队在周末的每一节练习中都证明了自己比竞争对手更胜一筹，并通过利用其转向优势锁定了前两排。
拉塞尔在决定性的Q3冲刺赛中，在第一轮和第二轮中分别跑出1m21.695s的成绩，领先他的世界冠军队友近两十分，并且明显领先其他竞争者。
安东内利质疑自己为何在最后一轮中排在第一位，这位意大利少年在第二次尝试中找不到任何改进，最终排名第二。拉塞尔几乎复制了他的第一次成绩，但无需改进就赢得了他本赛季第六个杆位，这对于他的成长之旅意义重大。
迈凯轮的兰多·诺里斯在第二轮中提高了十分，以第三名的成绩领先队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，而伊萨克·哈吉亚在排位赛中击败了他的红牛队友马克斯·维斯塔潘，获得了第五个发车位。
法拉利在多哈的糟糕周末继续，整个练习赛中都在为抓地力和速度而挣扎。查尔斯·勒克莱尔只能排在第七位，距离杆位有1.260秒的差距。青训车队小红牛的菜鸟车手阿维德·林德布拉德击败了刘易斯·汉密尔顿的第二辆法拉利，利亚姆·劳森以第十名的成绩结束了前十。
红牛车队在Q2的表现与梅赛德斯车队相当接近，哈德贾的成绩为1m22.344s，比领跑者拉塞尔慢不到三十分之一，拉塞尔以1m22.079s的成绩领先安东内利。
在这两支车队和梅赛德斯车队之后，法拉利再次陷入困境，勒克莱尔落后整整一秒，他们试图与小红牛车队抗衡。
尽管如此，两队仍有足够的余地进入Q3。对于前十名的争夺，哈斯、阿尔派和奥迪之间的竞争非常激烈，但最终这三支车队都没有足够的实力去威胁排名第十的劳森。
奥利弗·贝尔曼最接近，只差0.240s未能晋级。皮埃尔·加斯利从FP2中失去的时间中恢复过来，在发车位上获得第十二名，随后是加布里埃尔·博托莱托和他的队友弗朗哥·科拉平托。哈斯车队的新人拉斐尔·卡马拉和经验丰富的尼科·胡肯伯格将在周日的第八排发车。
梅赛德斯和红牛是唯一两支在Q1中只完成了一圈计时圈速的车队，拉塞尔的1分22.557秒领先，排在安东内利和维斯塔潘之前。其他领跑者虽然也在磨损的轮胎上完成了一圈，但同样也为稍后保留了关键的软胎。
第一轮练习结束后，卡洛斯·塞恩斯和亚历克斯·阿隆诺在圈外观望，威廉姆斯车手在第二轮练习后仍保持在这个位置。这对科拉平托来说是个安慰，他凭借0.1秒的优势从第16位惊险晋级Q1。与此同时，哈斯车队的新人卡马拉也晋级到第14位，但他为此不得不使用第二套软胎。
费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔分别以第19位和第20位为陷入困境的阿斯顿·马丁车队挣扎，凯迪拉克车队的瓦尔特里·博塔斯和塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯完成了周日的排位赛。
detailEn: F1 Qatar GP: George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole
George Russell takes sixth pole of 2026 as Mercedes dominates qualifying at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix
George Russell has grabbed an emphatic pole for Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, defeating team-mate Kimi Antonelli as Mercedes blitzed the competition in Doha.

On the demanding, high-downforce circuit of Lusail, Mercedes proved a step ahead of the competition in every session over the weekend, and the Silver Arrows capitalised on their cornering advantage by locking out the front row.
Russell led from Antonelli after the first of two runs in the decisive Q3 shootout with a 1m21.695s lap, nearly two tenths up on his world champion team-mate and well clear of the competition.

As Antonelli questioned being out first in the queue for the final runs, the Italian teenager struggled to find any improvement on his second attempt and settled for second. Russell almost matched his first run, but did not need to improve to claim his sixth pole of a character-building campaign.
McLaren's Lando Norris found a tenth on his second lap to claim third ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri, with Isack Hadjar out-qualifying his Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen for fifth on the grid.

Ferrari continued a woeful weekend in Doha, having been struggling for grip and pace throughout practice. Charles Leclerc could only manage seventh on the grid, a shocking 1.260s off pole. Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad beat the second Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton to eighth, with Liam Lawson rounding out the top 10.
Red Bull, rather than McLaren, looked somewhat close to Mercedes in Q2, with Hadjar's 1m22.344s less than three tenths behind pacesetter Russell, who had the edge on Antonelli with a 1m22.079s lap.
Behind those two teams and McLaren, Ferrari struggled again, with Leclerc a full second behind as they looked to fight with Racing Bulls.

There was still a big enough cushion for both teams to make it into Q3, though. The battle for the top-10 was a tight fight between Haas, Alpine and Audi, but ultimately none of the three teams had enough in the tank to bother 10th-placed Lawson.

Oliver Bearman came closest, missing the cut by 0.240s. Pierre Gasly recovered from lost track time in FP2 to take 12th on the grid, followed by Gabriel Bortoleto and team-mate Franco Colapinto. Haas rookie Rafael Camara and veteran Nico Hulkenberg will start from the eighth row on Sunday.

Mercedes and Red Bull were the only two teams to just set one timed lap in Q1, with Russell's 1m22.557s leading the way ahead of Antonelli and Verstappen. The other frontrunners set a second time on scrubbed tyres, though, equally saving crucial sets of softs for later on.

After the first set of runs, Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon were on the outside looking in and the Williams drivers stayed in those positions after the second effort. That was a relief for Colapinto, who escaped Q1 by a tenth of a second in 16th. Meanwhile, Haas rookie Camara also advanced in 14th, but had to deploy a second set of softs to do so in 14th.
Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll were 19th and 20th for struggling Aston Martin, with Cadillac duo Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez completing Sunday's grid.

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.
